## Cleaning the Data

Anaylzing how many values are missing inside the data set
```{r}

```

and year. I left it here in case we can use it at some point.

There's a lot of overlap on totals, years, months, states, genders, and the age groups. To help clean it up, I'm going to keep only the national totals by sex and another national total by 11 age groups.

```{r}
covid <- covid[covid$Group == "By Total" &
                     covid$State == "United States" &
                     covid$Sex != "All Sexes" &
                     covid$Age.Group != "All Ages" &
                     covid$Age.Group != "0-17 years" &
                     covid$Age.Group != "18-29 years" &
                     covid$Age.Group != "30-39 years" &
                     covid$Age.Group != "40-49 years" &
                     covid$Age.Group != "50-64 years", ]
dim(covid)
```



Fixing counts from being character into numeric.
```{r}
count_cols <- c("COVID.19.Deaths", "Total.Deaths", "Pneumonia.Deaths",
                "Pneumonia.and.COVID.19.Deaths")
covid <- covid[, c("Sex", "Age.Group", count_cols)]

for (col_name in count_cols) {
  covid[, col_name] <- clean_counts(covid[, col_name])
}
```

Removing rows with a missing count.

```{r}
n_obs <- nrow(covid)
missing <- rep(FALSE, n_obs)
for (obs_ind in 1:n_obs) {
  obs <- covid[obs_ind, count_cols]
  n_missing <- sum(is.na(obs))
  if (n_missing > 0) {
    missing[obs_ind] <- TRUE
  }
}
covid <- covid[!missing, ]
```

Final Checks on the dataset dimensions and missing rows.
```{r}
dim(covid)
sum(is.na(covid))
covid
```
